websiteToolStrengthLevel.title: Strength level calculator
websiteToolStrengthLevel.intro: Enter your body weight and a set you did. See which strength level your estimated one-rep max reaches for that lift, and how much each level needs at your body weight.

form.reserveHint: How many more reps you could have done. Leave empty if you went to failure.

problems.bodyWeight: Enter your body weight as a number above 0.
problems.weight: Enter the weight you lifted as a number above 0.
problems.reps: Enter the reps as a whole number from 1 to 10.
problems.repsTooHigh: Sets above 10 reps do not give a trustworthy one-rep max. A long set measures endurance, and every formula drifts further from the truth the more reps it has to extrapolate. Use a heavier set of 10 reps or fewer.
problems.reserve: Reps in reserve must be a whole number from 0 to 9.

results.otherNote: Shown on both the men's and women's scales, because no single table fits.
results.nextLevel: To reach {{level}}: an estimated one-rep max of {{weight}} {{unit}}.
results.topLevel: This lift is at the top level. There is no level above elite.
results.tableTitle: The one-rep max each level needs at your body weight
results.tableNote: Each figure is the estimated one-rep max for this lift at your body weight.

sections.title: What the level compares
body: A level is your estimated one-rep max divided by your body weight, adjusted for the lift and for sex. Heavier people lift more in total, so the body weight is part of the comparison.
Levels are a Musclog rule of thumb, checked against public powerlifting results from OpenPowerlifting. They show where a lift sits on that scale. They do not rank you against other people.

sections.title: Why sex and the lift change the numbers
body: The benchmark for a lift depends on its body region, and women's results sit lower against body weight in the public data, so a woman's level uses a lower benchmark for that region.
Choose Other when you do not want the answer on one scale. Both the men's and women's scales are shown, and a range is given when they grade differently.

sections.title: Dumbbell lifts
body: Dumbbell lifts are graded per hand, because both the benchmark and the weight you log are per hand. Enter the weight of one dumbbell, not the pair.
